Technology stocks were firming in recent trading Thursday, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.9% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was more up than 0.3%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Avalara Inc ( AVLR ) raced almost 12% on Thursday after the maker of business-tax compliance software said its Avalara TrustFile software suite was available on Amazon.com's ( AMZN ) marketplace appstore and now gaining access to other companies that sell products or services on the e-commerce giant and helping them focus more of their time on business and less on sales tax filings and compliance issues.
In other sector news:
+ Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) climbed almost 6% on Thursday, stopping only 28 cents shy of its 52-week high of $46.37 a share after reporting fiscal Q4 financial results exceeding analyst estimates and forecast Q1 earnings and revenue growth also topping Wall Street expectations on the success of its new Catalyst series, application growth and continued strength in security. The network equipment company earned $0.70 per share on $12.8 billion in revenue during the May-to-July reporting period, topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.01 per share and $60 million, respectively.
+ JD.com ( JD ) was nearly 1% higher Thursday afternoon, recovering from a nearly 4% drop to a 16-month low of $31.19 per American depositary share after its Q2 profit fell almost 50% compared with year-ago levels and missed Wall Street forecasts. Excluding one-time items, the Chineses e-commerce company earned $0.05 per ADS, down from $0.097 per ADS profit last year and also trailing the $0.10 per ADS analyst mean. Net sales rose 32% year over year to $18.5 billion, topping the Capital IQ consensus expecting $17.8 billion. It also sees Q3 sales trailing analyst projections.
